extracted.intended_audience: Potential applicants to EPA STAR grants (academic institutions, hospitals, state/local governments, Tribes, non-profit research institutions, students, and research scientists)
extracted.subtask_description: A program-level overview of EPA's Science to Achieve Results (STAR) extramural research grants, including who is eligible, the kinds of research funded, and program characteristics (competitive, peer-reviewed). Useful for prospective applicants seeking whether they, and their proposed research, fit the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible applicants under the STAR program
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible applicants under the STAR program include academic institutions, hospitals, state/local governments, Tribes, and other non-profit research institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit eligibility criterion: applicants must be one of the listed entity types to apply under STAR. (Original wording: 'Eligible applicants under the STAR program include academic institutions, hospitals, state/local governments, Tribes, and other non-profit research institutions.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Research topics funded by STAR
rubrics_metrics.description: The program funds research on environmental and public health effects of air pollution, water quality and quantity, hazardous waste, toxic substances, pesticides and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should propose work falling within STAR's topical scope. The site further organizes funding into research-area pages (Air, Climate Change, Ecosystems, Health, Safer Chemicals, Sustainability, Water), indicating the main thematic areas supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program is competitive and peer-reviewed
rubrics_metrics.description: STAR is EPA's primary competitive, peer-reviewed extramural grant program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals will be evaluated through competitive, peer-review processes; the program has awarded over 4,100 grants since 1995. Applicants should prepare proposals suited to peer review (clear hypotheses/objectives, rigorous methods, strong justification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with EPA mission / purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should result in a strong scientific foundation to support the agency's mission of protecting human health and the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed work should be framed to demonstrate how it supports EPA's mission and addresses high-priority environmental and public health research needs. Alignment with agency priorities is implied as a criterion for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target participants and engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA funds extramural research grants to engage top research scientists, non-profit organizations, students, and others in research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program seeks to leverage scientific and engineering expertise from academic and non-profit institutions; proposals that involve qualified investigators, training/mentorship elements, or institutional partnerships are consistent with program aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult current opportunities and contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are directed to 'See open grant opportunities under the STAR program' and to contact EPA about research grants via provided contact links and a Research Grants Listserv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is procedural guidance: prospective applicants should consult the active open opportunities for specific solicitations, deadlines, and detailed requirements, and may use the contact channels or listserv to ask questions or report problems.
